title: Chinese state TV suspends La Liga broadcasts after Mbappé remark about Mao
seoTitle: Mbappé China row: La Liga broadcasts suspended
dek: China's state broadcaster stopped showing La Liga after a video in which Kylian Mbappé described a meme of himself as showing a "Chinese dictator". Three Chinese brands ended their deals with him; he has apologised.
happened: A behind-the-scenes clip, filmed in April and posted by the French podcast The Bridge on 26 October, showed the Real Madrid forward saying the funniest meme he had seen put his face on "some guy – I think he's a Chinese dictator". The meme showed Mao Zedong; Mbappé did not name him. China Media Group, which runs state broadcaster CCTV, suspended La Liga broadcasts and adverts featuring Mbappé. Eastroc Beverage (Dongpeng), dairy company Mengniu and cheesemaker Milkground ended their partnerships with him.

sides.says: In a statement in French, English and Mandarin, he called his comment "ill-judged", said he has "deep respect for the Chinese people and their history" and apologised "to everyone my words have upset".

sides.who: China's foreign ministry and China Media Group
sides.says: Before the apology, a foreign ministry spokesperson said words that hurt the feelings of Chinese people "will naturally be met with opposition". Afterwards the ministry said it took the apology seriously. China Media Group said the remarks "crossed fundamental boundaries" and that the dispute would not be settled without a satisfactory apology from the club.
The club apologised to the Chinese people for "any discomfort caused" and said Mbappé had not meant to cause offence.

League president Javier Tebas met China's ambassador to Spain to look for a way past the episode, writing that a relationship built over many years "cannot be damaged by a single incident". Reports differ on whether he apologised.

next: As of 28 October, China Media Group had not said when La Liga broadcasts would resume. Reuters reported that Tebas was considering a trip to China.
summary: The row began when a clip of Kylian Mbappé, recorded in April, spread on social media on 26 October. In it he said a meme of his face had been put on "some guy – I think he's a Chinese dictator"; the image was of Mao Zedong. China Media Group, the state media group that runs CCTV, suspended La Liga broadcasts and pulled adverts featuring the Real Madrid forward. Three Chinese companies ended their partnerships with him; according to Le Monde, the Dongpeng and Mengniu contracts were worth about 50 million yuan (€6.7 million) combined. Several international brands removed Mbappé content from their Weibo accounts. Mbappé apologised in three languages, Real Madrid apologised to the Chinese people, and La Liga's president met China's ambassador to Spain. China Media Group said the club's explanation was not enough and named no date for broadcasts to resume.
